head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Restrict MultiPhaseFusion to chains of stages, i.e. disallow concurrent stages for now.

MultiPhaseFusion was generalized to DAGs before, however, DAGs with wide fan-outs / lots of independent stages are an issue. Currently, MultiPhaseFusion will sequenialize such wide fan-out DAGs, which increases compile times and renders downstream HorizontalFusion infeasible. The desired end state is supporting spatial partitioned concurrent execution of independent stages (up to the thread block cluster limit) within MultiPhaseFusions.

For now, require every stage added in `TryAddStage` to be reachability-ordered with all existing stages in the candidate DAG, keeping `BuildPhaseDag` intact so this
check can be replaced by an ALAP list scheduler later.

display_title: Avoid double-pushing tombstones in HloComputation constructor

head_commit.message:
Avoid double-pushing tombstones in HloComputation constructor

When `HloComputation` is constructed with `preserve_instruction_ids=true` (such as from `HloComputation::CreateFromProto` on a computation containing deleted-instruction local ID gaps), it pre-allocates `instructions_.resize(max_instruction_local_id + 1)`, which already populates every gap index with an empty `HloInstructionInfo`. However, the subsequent loop still calls `instructions_.push_back(HloInstructionInfo())` for every `nullptr` entry in `*instructions`. This appends `num_gaps` duplicate trailing tombstones to `instructions_` and inflates `next_instruction_unique_id_` by `num_gaps`, shifting the `local_id` and `unique_id` of every instruction subsequently added to the computation.

Initialize `next_instruction_unique_id_` to `instructions_.size()` after pre-allocating for `preserve_instruction_ids=true`, and replace the `push_back` on `nullptr` entries with `CHECK(preserve_instruction_ids)` since `nullptr` gaps only arise when pre-allocating preserved IDs (`Builder::Build` dereferences every entry and `CreateFromProto` always passes `preserve_instruction_ids=true`).

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Support shift operations in the Triton/XTile block-level emitter

Closes a feature gap between the block-level (Triton/XTile) emitter and the
native reduction emitters by enabling `shift-left`, `shift-right-logical`, and
`shift-right-arithmetic` across all Triton-supported integral types (`S8`,
`S16`, `S32`, `S64`, `U8`, `U16`, `U32`, `U64`). Previously, fusions containing
shift operations (such as reductions over shifted inputs) were rejected during
Triton support checking as unsupported elementwise operations.

### Summary of Changes
- **Support check** (`xla/backends/gpu/codegen/triton/support.cc`): Enable
  `kShiftLeft`, `kShiftRightArithmetic`, and `kShiftRightLogical` in
  `TritonSupportedBinaryElementwiseOps` for integral types (excluding `S4`/`U4`
  and `PRED`).
- **XTile emission & verification** (`xla/codegen/xtile/codegen/emitter_helpers.cc`,
  `xla/codegen/xtile/ir/transforms/verify_legal_xtile_ops.cc`): Emit and allow
  `stablehlo.shift_left`, `stablehlo.shift_right_logical`, and
  `stablehlo.shift_right_arithmetic`.
- **StableHLO-to-Arith lowering** (`xla/codegen/xtile/ir/transforms/lower_stablehlo_to_arith.cc`):
  Lower all three shift ops to `arith.shli` / `arith.shrui` / `arith.shrsi`
  (converting unsigned operands to signless as needed) while preserving XLA's
  defined saturation semantics for out-of-bounds shift amounts
  (`arith.cmpi ult, rhs, bitwidth`): saturate to `0` for `shift-left` and
  `shift-right-logical`, and to `arith.shrsi(lhs, bitwidth - 1)` for
  `shift-right-arithmetic`. Performing this lowering directly in
  `StablehloLowerToArithPass` keeps the IR immediately sound before
  canonicalization and lets constant shift amounts fold away cleanly.
- **Tests**: Add FileCheck lowering tests in
  `xla/codegen/xtile/ir/transforms/tests/lower_stablehlo_to_arith.mlir` and
  GPU execution tests covering out-of-bounds/negative shift amounts and
  shift+reduction fusions in
  `xla/backends/gpu/codegen/triton/tests/fusion_emitter_device_test.cc`.

display_title: [re-land #2][xla:cpu] add full msan support

head_commit.message:
[re-land #2][xla:cpu] add full msan support

Msan support is currently incomplete.  For example, we don't add
the appropriate msan pass to LLVM's pipeline; instead, we manually
call __msan_unpoison here and there. In AOT (tfcompile) the situation
is even worse, since we only add these annotations to some of the
emitted code.

This change adds complete support for msan (and msan-track-origins)
to XLA:CPU in both JIT and AOT modes. In particular:

- Adds a single boolean config flag to determine whether msan should
  be enabled in compiled code. This is then wired up through the
  compiler, removing several #ifdef MEMORY_SANITIZER (or equivalent)
  checks that we had scattered around the code base. (OK, this is
  two knobs because we also support track-origins.)
- Adds the msan pass to LLVM as documented in
    https://github.com/google/sanitizers/wiki/MemorySanitizerJIT
  This requires a small TLS emulation library, which (1) in JIT
  gives access to host symbols from JIT'ed code, and (2) in AOT
  (tfcompile) must be linked in the final binary so that the
  compiled code can reliably access msan symbols.

A couple of upstream LLVM bugs (fixes are under review) require
some workarounds:
- Disable SVE on AArch64 when msan is enabled, since LLVM's
  MemorySanitizer can't handle scalable vectors yet.
- Disable AVX2 on x86 hosts without AVX512BW+VLX when msan is
  enabled, since LLVM's X86 backend can't select bf16 broadcasts
  there yet.

What's missing from this CL:
1. Removal of now obsolete annotations
2. Setting of the appropriate flags in tfcompile to enable the
  new path in AOT.

These two missing changes will land once users have had time to recompile
their compilers (in case they embed tfcompile into them), about
1-2 weeks.

Note: the msan support implemented in this CL supersedes
https://github.com/openxla/xla/commit/70f2607611. That means the
xla_backend_extra option added there for msan on AOT will be removed when
landing the two missing pieces from this CL.

Reverts 3b900dd1a9e09783eec4a910220dfad75f068f3c

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Return 0 latency for non-async edges in GpuLatencyEstimator.

`GpuLatencyEstimator::GetLatencyBetween` returned `kLowLatency` (1.0) for non-async edges. During bottom-up scheduling, any node with `NodeCost < 1.0` (0-cost NOPs such as `bitcast` and `get-tuple-element`, or sub-microsecond ops under `SolLatencyEstimator` and `ProfileGuidedLatencyEstimator`) therefore created an artificial stall on its predecessor. Because `kLessStall` outranks `kAsyncDepth` and `kUnlockDone`, independent 0-async-depth ops beat the critical path and got pinned outside async collective windows.

Return 0.0 for non-async edges while keeping positive latencies on async start-to-done pairs. Adds regression tests for both paths and updates the H100 AOT compatibility golden for `reduction_collectives_aot_test_2gpu_h100`.

GPU FFI handlers such as Triton kernels with zeroed outputs or custom collectives often need to zero output or scratch buffers before launching a kernel. [XLA:CPU] Test YNNPACK fusion exp near FLT_MIN/DBL_MIN under FTZ.

`YnnUnaryOpTest` tests `exponential` with nonzero absolute tolerances (`2e-38` for `f32`, `2e-308` for `f64`), which mask large relative errors in the lowest normal binades when flush-to-zero (FTZ) is enabled. head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fold index_cast chains in ConvertIndexTypePass.

After `ConvertIndexTypePass` rewrites `index` arithmetic to fixed-width integers, `arith.index_cast(arith.index_cast(x : iN) : index) : iM` chains with `N != M` remain because MLIR's built-in canonicalizer only folds when `N == M` without a known `index` bitwidth. Downstream passes such as Triton's `AxisInfoAnalysis` have no visitor for `arith.index_cast`, which resets offset divisibility to 1 and prevents 128-bit vectorized loads on `dynamic-slice` kernels.

Add `FoldIndexCastChain` to `ConvertIndexTypePass` using the module's DataLayout `index` bitwidth to fold signless `iN -> index(B) -> iM` chains into direct `arith.extsi`, `arith.trunci`, or identity ops (and `arith.trunci` followed by `arith.extsi` when both `N > B` and `M > B`).

Fusions containing `dynamic-slice` with unsigned integer start indices (`u8`, `u16`, `u32`, `u64`) previously fell back to the native emitters because `IsTritonSupportedDynamicSlice` rejected unsigned index types and `EmitClampedIndex` lowered clamping through signless `arith.maxsi`/`arith.minsi`.

display_title: PR #53878: [XLA:GPU] Create reduce-scatter through elementwise ops between all-reduce and dynamic-slice

head_commit.message:
PR #53878: [XLA:GPU] Create reduce-scatter through elementwise ops between all-reduce and dynamic-slice

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53878

📝 Summary of Changes

`ReduceScatterCreator` converts `dynamic-slice(all-reduce(x))` into a `reduce-scatter`, but only when the dynamic-slice consumes the all-reduce directly (or through a reshape). This change lets it also handle the case where copies and elementwise operations with scalar-broadcast operands sit between the two:

```
all-reduce -> multiply(broadcast(scalar)) -> copy -> dynamic-slice
```

`MatchReduceScatter` gets a new option, `allow_intervening_elementwise`, next to the existing options for an intervening reshape or bitcast. With it, the dynamic-slice is also found through such a chain, which is returned in `ReduceScatterSpec::intervening_elementwise`. The option is off by default, so other users of the matcher are not affected.

`ReduceScatterCreator` enables the option. After a successful match it creates the reduce-scatter and re-creates the intermediate operations on its result:

```
reduce-scatter -> multiply(broadcast(scalar)) -> copy
```

For example, with 8 replicas and `%offset` selecting the shard of the current replica (`replica-id * 4`):

```
// Before
%all-reduce  = f32[32,8,128] all-reduce(%param), replica_groups={}, to_apply=%sum
%scale_bcast = f32[32,8,128] broadcast(%scale), dimensions={}
%scaled      = f32[32,8,128] multiply(%all-reduce, %scale_bcast)
%copy        = f32[32,8,128] copy(%scaled)
ROOT %dynamic-slice = f32[4,8,128] dynamic-slice(%copy, %offset, %zero, %zero), dynamic_slice_sizes={4,8,128}

// After
%reduce-scatter = f32[4,8,128] reduce-scatter(%param), replica_groups={}, dimensions={0}, to_apply=%sum
%scale_bcast    = f32[4,8,128] broadcast(%scale), dimensions={}
%scaled         = f32[4,8,128] multiply(%reduce-scatter, %scale_bcast)
ROOT %copy      = f32[4,8,128] copy(%scaled)
```

The module is only modified when a reduce-scatter is created. The rewrite is exact, since slicing commutes with per-element operations. The chain is only matched when neither the all-reduce nor an instruction in the chain is the root of its computation, and every instruction in the chain has a single user, has no side effects or control dependencies, preserves the dimensions, and is a copy or another elementwise operation (not a fusion) whose other operands are broadcasts of scalars to the same dimensions, without control dependencies. The re-created instructions keep the layout of the original ones.

🎯 Justification

The SPMD partitioner emits this chain for scaled weight gradients: the gradient is all-reduced across a mesh axis, multiplied by a scalar, and then sliced to the shard of the current partition. Because of the multiply, the full-size all-reduce was left in place and every device received the complete tensor only to discard all but its own shard.

In MaxText Kimi K2 (1T parameters, MoE, FP8) training, each of the 60 scanned layers all-reduces three `bf16[48,7168,2048]` expert-weight gradients (1.4 GB each) across the 32-way FSDP axis and then slices them to `[48,224,2048]`. These all-reduces accounted for about 10 s of a 30.7 s training step. With this change they become reduce-scatters, and the scalar multiply and copy run on the 44 MB shard instead of the 1.4 GB tensor.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

⚡️ Performance Improvement

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

MaxText training with FP8 quantization on B200 GPUs, average step time over steps 40-60, one run per configuration. The 2-node rows use 5 decoder layers, FSDP across the 2 nodes (`dcn_fsdp_parallelism=2`) and expert parallelism within a node (`ici_expert_parallelism=8`).

| Model              | Configuration                        | Before (s/step) | After (s/step) | Change  |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------ | --------------- | -------------- | ------- |
| Kimi K2 (1T)       | Full model, 32 nodes x 8 (256 GPUs)  | 30.70           | 25.78          | -16.0%  |
| Kimi K2 (1T)       | 5 layers, 2 nodes x 8, seq 2048      | 1.4286          | 1.2592         | -11.9%  |
| DeepSeek-V3 671B   | 5 layers, 2 nodes x 8, seq 2048      | 0.5250          | 0.4703         | -10.4%  |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 671B | 5 layers, 2 nodes x 8, seq 4096      | 0.7779          | 0.7226         | -7.1%   |

🧪 Unit Tests:

Thirteen tests added to `reduce_scatter_creator_test.cc`. Conversions: through a scalar multiply and a copy, through a type conversion, through a clamp with two scalar-broadcast bounds, for a cross-partition all-reduce, and through a copy of a sub-byte type, whose layout is kept. Left unchanged: the other multiply operand is not a scalar broadcast, the scaled result has a second user, the multiply or its scalar broadcast has a control dependency, the bounds of a clamp are rank-0 broadcasts, or the all-reduce or the multiply is the root of the computation. Also left unchanged: a chain whose slice offsets do not select per-device shards. Six tests added to `collective_opt_utils_test.cc` for the new matcher option: the chain is found only when the option is set, and a non-scalar operand, a reshape after the chain, an elementwise fusion, and a collective or chain instruction that is the computation root are rejected. Both test targets pass, as do the tests of the other passes that use the matcher (all-reduce splitter, collective pipelining analyzer and the all-gather dynamic-slice simplifiers).

🧪 Execution Tests:

all-reduce directly (or through a reshape). The SPMD partitioner can emit
all-reduce -> multiply by a scalar -> copy -> dynamic-slice, for example
for scaled weight gradients, which left a full-size all-reduce in place.

feeding the intermediate elementwise operations are re-created with the sliced
shape. A new broadcast does not carry the control dependencies of the original
one, so the ordering they express would be lost. Leave such chains unchanged
and add a test.

[XLA:GPU] Follow XLA style guidelines in the reduce-scatter slice sinking

- Return xla::Decision from the helpers that decide whether a dynamic-slice
  can be moved above an instruction, and log the explanation when it cannot.
- Use absl::c_all_of for the check of the remaining operands.
- Do not move the dynamic-slice when a shape in the chain is dynamic, as the
  re-created instructions get static shapes.

[XLA:GPU] Match elementwise ops in MatchReduceScatter instead of moving the dynamic-slice first

ReduceScatterCreator moved the dynamic-slice next to the all-reduce before
matching, which changed the module even when no reduce-scatter was created
afterwards.

Add allow_intervening_elementwise to MatchReduceScatter, MatchWithDynamicSlice
and FindUniqueDynamicSliceUserFromCollective, next to the existing options for
an intervening reshape or bitcast. With it, the dynamic-slice is also found
through a chain of single-user copies and elementwise operations whose other
operands are scalar broadcasts, and the chain is returned in
ReduceScatterSpec::intervening_elementwise. The option is off by default, so
other users of the matcher are not affected.

creates the reduce-scatter and re-creates the intermediate operations on its
result.

[XLA:GPU] Do not look through fusions or computation roots when matching elementwise ops for reduce-scatter

Address review comments on the elementwise chain between an all-reduce and
its dynamic-slice:

- Check the opcode with HloInstruction::IsOpElementwise instead of
  IsElementwise(), which also holds for elementwise fusions. A fusion cannot
  be re-created with a different shape, as its fused computation keeps the
  original shapes.
- Do not match a chain if the all-reduce or one of the chain instructions is

head_commit.message:
PR #52971: [AlgebraicSimplifier] Gate constant reciprocal division rewrite on fast math

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52971

#ai-generated

Fixes #52968.

## Status quo

`HandleDivide` rewrites floating-point division by a constant into multiplication by a rounded reciprocal, including when `enable_fast_math` is false.

## Why

We encountered this while comparing an ONNX quantized MLP across execution backends. For float32 `[-100, 0.1, 100]`, the scale `200 / 255` changes by one ULP. The subsequent zero-point calculation crosses a rounding boundary, producing 127 instead of 128. The issue includes an independent JAX reproduction with CPU fast math disabled.

## Design choices

Require `enable_fast_math` for this rewrite. Add scalar and broadcasted-constant tests with fast math disabled, and explicitly enable fast math in the existing reciprocal-rewrite tests.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Emit embedded CustomKernelThunks for CUDA CUB sorts

Previously, XLA lowered CUDA CUB sorts to FFI custom calls backed by `cub::DeviceRadixSort` and `cub::DeviceSegmentedRadixSort` in the runtime, and relied on precomputed per-device scratch size lookup tables for deviceless compilation. That tied the GPU runtime to CUB host APIs and broke deviceless compilation whenever a GPU model, CCCL version, or tensor shape was missing from the checked-in tables.

So this change wires the compiler-owned CUB sort planner and native custom-call handler into the CUDA compilation pipeline. `EstimateCubSortScratchSize` now computes CUDA scratch sizes directly in pure C++ from the target compute capability (for both live-GPU and deviceless compilation), `SortRewriter` rewrites compatible CUDA sorts without consulting lookup tables, and `nvptx_compiler_impl` links `cub_sort_thunk_emitter_registration` so `ThunkEmitter` lowers `xla.gpu.ext.cub_sort_{keys,pairs}` via `NativeCustomCallHandlerRegistry` directly into embedded `CustomKernelThunk` sequences.

This removes the compile-time scratch query and runtime CUB host-API dependency for newly compiled CUDA executables, removes the per-call H2D offset copy on batched sorts, and lets CUDA CUB sorts participate in command buffers. The legacy `kCubSort{Keys,Pairs}Execute` FFI handlers remain in `xla/stream_executor/cuda/cub_sort_kernel_cuda.cc` for 6-month AOT backward compatibility (scheduled for removal after May 2027), while the obsolete CUDA instantiate and dummy-execute handlers are removed.

display_title: `DynamicPadder` miscompiles or crashes on several bounded-dynamic HLO shapes across CPU, GPU, and TPU:

head_commit.message:
`DynamicPadder` miscompiles or crashes on several bounded-dynamic HLO shapes across CPU, GPU, and TPU:

- Variadic `kScatter` only pads operand 1 instead of `scatter_indices`, and pads narrow indices with `MaxValue` even when in bounds while leaving `indices_are_sorted` set for negative padding.
- `kSelectAndScatter` accepts any `kGe` compare, miscompiling reversed or reflexive comparators and mishandling `kLe`, complex types, and float `TOTALORDER`.
- `kDot`, `kConvolution`, and dynamic convolution custom calls pad with operand 0 or output zero instead of each operand's type, accept `F8E8M0FNU` and auxiliary operands, and drop sliced `DynamicConvolutionInputGrad` `precision_config`.
- `RewriteDynamicSort` mutates tuple sort arity in place and breaks shardings, control dependencies, and sub-byte layouts.
- `RewriteDynamicUpdateSlice` clamps partial updates at `N - B` instead of `N - d` (or `base_dyn - d`).
- Zero-bound dynamic reshapes, zero-bound or over-`INT32_MAX` dynamic reverses, and unbounded `get-dimension-size` fail verification or truncate bounds.

Fix all six cases directly in `dynamic_padder.cc` without changing static modules.

Tests:
- `//third_party/tensorflow/compiler/xla/tests:dynamic_padder_test`: covers variadic and narrow-index scatter, min/max select-and-scatter, mixed-type dot and dynamic convolution, variadic sharded sort, right-edge clamped dynamic-update-slice, and zero-bound or unbounded shapes.

head_commit.message:
Validate dimensions before narrowing in SelectKExecuteFfiHandler.

`SelectKExecuteFfiHandler` previously cast `int64_t` input and output dimensions directly to `uint32_t` without bounds checks. Malformed `__gpu$TopK` shapes could trigger divide-by-zero in RAFT `warpsort::calc_launch_parameter` when `batch` or `n` is zero. Oversized shapes could silently truncate on cast or wrap 32-bit `batch * k`, causing out-of-bounds GPU writes in `segmented_sort_by_key`.

Validate `batch`, `n`, and `k` in `int64_t` before narrowing to `uint32_t`, matching the invariants in `EstimateRaftSelectKScratchBytesImpl`. Reject non-positive dimensions, `k > n`, `batch` or `n` exceeding `INT32_MAX`, and `batch * k` exceeding `UINT32_MAX` with `InvalidArgumentError`.

display_title: [XLA] Fix DotMerger crashes, attribute conflation, and overflow bugs

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Fix DotMerger crashes, attribute conflation, and overflow bugs

- Stop walking through `bitcast`, sharded, tagged, dynamic, or control
  dependent operand and consumer instructions, and preserve nondefault layouts
  feeding `bitcast` and computation roots.
- Skip dead, sparse, block scaled, scalar operand, dynamic, zero element, and
  tiled or named sharded dots.
- Key merge equivalence on raw backend config, bitwise `result_accuracy`, side
  relative operand precision and algorithm, and replicated or manual sharding,
  and propagate them across merged instructions and post-slice chains.
- Use `absl::int128` in `FindDotsToMerge` cost and merged byte bound checks and
  guard nonpositive runtime estimates.

display_title: [xla:cpu] record msan instrumentation in AOT results and check it on load

head_commit.message:
[xla:cpu] record msan instrumentation in AOT results and check it on load

The object files in an AOT result only work in processes with the same msan
instrumentation. Elsewhere, instrumented code fails to load with an unhelpful

  Symbols not found: [ __msan_init, __msan_warning_noreturn ]

while uninstrumented code in an msan process silently escapes msan's checks.

Record the instrumentation in CompilationResultProto, and make CpuAotLoader
reject results whose instrumentation differs from the process's. Results that
predate the new fields count as uninstrumented, which they are, so they keep
loading in processes without msan.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1031314033

display_title: [re-land #2][xla:cpu] add full msan support

head_commit.message:
[re-land #2][xla:cpu] add full msan support

Msan support is currently incomplete.  For example, we don't add
the appropriate msan pass to LLVM's pipeline; instead, we manually
call __msan_unpoison here and there. In AOT (tfcompile) the situation
is even worse, since we only add these annotations to some of the
emitted code.

This change adds complete support for msan (and msan-track-origins)
to XLA:CPU in both JIT and AOT modes. In particular:

- Adds a single boolean config flag to determine whether msan should
  be enabled in compiled code. This is then wired up through the
  compiler, removing several #ifdef MEMORY_SANITIZER (or equivalent)
  checks that we had scattered around the code base. (OK, this is
  two knobs because we also support track-origins.)
- Adds the msan pass to LLVM as documented in
    https://github.com/google/sanitizers/wiki/MemorySanitizerJIT
  This requires a small TLS emulation library, which (1) in JIT
  gives access to host symbols from JIT'ed code, and (2) in AOT
  (tfcompile) must be linked in the final binary so that the
  compiled code can reliably access msan symbols.

A couple of upstream LLVM bugs (fixes are under review) require
some workarounds:
- Disable SVE on AArch64 when msan is enabled, since LLVM's
  MemorySanitizer can't handle scalable vectors yet.
- Disable AVX2 on x86 hosts without AVX512BW+VLX when msan is
  enabled, since LLVM's X86 backend can't select bf16 broadcasts
  there yet.

What's missing from this CL:
1. Removal of now obsolete annotations
2. Setting of the appropriate flags in tfcompile to enable the
  new path in AOT.

These two missing changes will land once users have had time to recompile
their compilers (in case they embed tfcompile into them), about
1-2 weeks.

Note: the msan support implemented in this CL supersedes
https://github.com/openxla/xla/commit/70f2607611. That means the
xla_backend_extra option added there for msan on AOT will be removed when
landing the two missing pieces from this CL.

Reverts 3b900dd1a9e09783eec4a910220dfad75f068f3c

`xla/service/gpu/gpu_norm_runner.{h,cc,proto}` only served `NormThunk` and `ThunkEmitter::EmitNorm`; unlike `gpu_conv_runner`, there is no norm autotuner sharing the runner layer, leaving `RunNormOptions::profile_result` unused and duplicating per-device `call_once` synchronization between `PerDeviceState` and `LazyOpRunner<NormOp>`.

display_title: [XLA] Make MatchAllGatherDynamicSliceOffset output deterministic

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Make MatchAllGatherDynamicSliceOffset output deterministic

`MatchAllGatherDynamicSliceOffset` in `xla/service/collective_opt_utils.cc` copied the already-ordered `absl::btree_map` (`ag_offset_map`) into an unordered `absl::flat_hash_map` before emitting `permutation_pairs`. Because `absl::flat_hash_map` randomizes iteration order per process, `AllGatherDynamicSlicePermutedOffsetSimplifier` emitted `collective-permute` `source_target_pairs` in a different order on every host during multi-host compilation, causing `HloModule::GetFingerprint128()` to diverge across hosts and deadlocking sharded GPU autotuning in `ConfigAssigner` KV-store synchronization.

Iterate directly over `ag_offset_map`, sort `spec.permutation_pairs` into canonical ascending `(source, target)` order (documented in `xla/service/collective_opt_utils.h`), and tighten/expand unit tests in `collective_opt_utils_test.cc` and `all_gather_permuted_ds_simplifier_test.cc` to assert deterministic pair ordering (including non-ascending replica groups and missing DS offsets).

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1031283664

head_commit.message:
[re-land #2][xla:cpu] add full msan support

Msan support is currently incomplete.  For example, we don't add
the appropriate msan pass to LLVM's pipeline; instead, we manually
call __msan_unpoison here and there. In AOT (tfcompile) the situation
is even worse, since we only add these annotations to some of the
emitted code.

This change adds complete support for msan (and msan-track-origins)
to XLA:CPU in both JIT and AOT modes. In particular:

- Adds a single boolean config flag to determine whether msan should
  be enabled in compiled code. This is then wired up through the
  compiler, removing several #ifdef MEMORY_SANITIZER (or equivalent)
  checks that we had scattered around the code base. (OK, this is
  two knobs because we also support track-origins.)
- Adds the msan pass to LLVM as documented in
    https://github.com/google/sanitizers/wiki/MemorySanitizerJIT
  This requires a small TLS emulation library, which (1) in JIT
  gives access to host symbols from JIT'ed code, and (2) in AOT
  (tfcompile) must be linked in the final binary so that the
  compiled code can reliably access msan symbols.

A couple of upstream LLVM bugs (fixes are under review) require
some workarounds:
- Disable SVE on AArch64 when msan is enabled, since LLVM's
  MemorySanitizer can't handle scalable vectors yet.
- Disable AVX2 on x86 hosts without AVX512BW+VLX when msan is
  enabled, since LLVM's X86 backend can't select bf16 broadcasts
  there yet.

What's missing from this CL:
1. Removal of now obsolete annotations
2. Setting of the appropriate flags in tfcompile to enable the
  new path in AOT.

These two missing changes will land once users have had time to recompile
their compilers (in case they embed tfcompile into them), about
1-2 weeks.

Note: the msan support implemented in this CL supersedes
https://github.com/openxla/xla/commit/70f2607611. That means the
xla_backend_extra option added there for msan on AOT will be removed when
landing the two missing pieces from this CL.

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Do not offload 8-bit integer arithmetic to YNNPACK

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Do not offload 8-bit integer arithmetic to YNNPACK

With default flags, porting a `uint8` image pipeline to JAX on CPU gives
results that differ from NumPy and XLA:GPU as soon as the inputs are large
enough to be fused into a `__ynn_fusion`. For example:

```python
f = jax.jit(lambda a, b: jnp.max(a, axis=0, keepdims=True) + b)
f(np.full((1024, 17), 255, np.uint8), np.full((1024, 17), 103, np.uint8))
```

returns `255` instead of `102`, and in a `uint8` contrast stretch 50-89% of
the pixels on 480x640 frames are wrong. `s8` `127 + 1` gives `127` instead of
`-128`, and `s8` `7 / 2` gives `4` instead of `3`. XLA:GPU, NumPy,
`HloEvaluator`, constant folding and XLA:CPU on small (unfused) inputs all
wrap and truncate.

Reported by @SomyaPadhy4501 in https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/51826
(found while porting an image pipeline, and also by a CPU-vs-GPU integer
fuzzer).

Root cause: `IsElementwiseOpSupportedByYnn` accepts `S8`/`U8` for every op in
`GetYnnBinaryOpMap()` and `GetYnnUnaryOpMap()`. YNNPACK's 8-bit add, subtract,
multiply and power saturate and its integer divide rounds. It has no 8-bit
unary kernels, so it computes them in fp32 and saturates the result (`u8`
`negate(1)` gives `0`, `s8` `negate(-128)` and `abs(-128)` give `127`). Any of
these ops fused next to a YNN reduction (the default `REDUCE` fusion type)
changes the result.

Fix: for `S8`/`U8` binary ops, only offload `maximum` and `minimum`, and for
`S8`/`U8` unary ops, only offload `convert` and `sign`. These give the same
results either way. Other 8-bit elementwise ops fall back to the regular
XLA:CPU emitter. Floating-point ops, integer reductions and converts are
unchanged. This follows the earlier fixes that stop offloading ops
YNNPACK cannot compute exactly (#48378, #49899).

Tested: new `YnnReduceInt8EltwiseTest.EltwiseAfterReduceWraps` in
`//xla/backends/cpu/transforms:ynn_matcher_test` runs the issue's pattern
(max/min reduce + broadcast + add/subtract/multiply/divide/power on `u8`/`s8`
`[1024,17]`), and new `YnnReduceInt8UnaryTest.UnaryBeforeReduceWraps` runs
`negate`/`abs` feeding a max reduce. All 9 cases fail before this change (255
vs 102, 127 vs -128, 0 vs 255, 127 vs -56, 4 vs 3, 127 vs -128, 0 vs 255, 127
vs -128, 127 vs -128) and pass after it. Both tests also check with
`MatchOptimizedHlo` that only the reduce stays in `__ynn_fusion`.
`YnnReduceTest.Int8MaximumAfterReduceIsFused` checks that `s8` maximum is
still fused into `__ynn_fusion`.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Restrict MultiPhaseFusion to chains of stages, i.e. disallow concurrent stages for now.

MultiPhaseFusion was generalized to DAGs before, however, DAGs with wide fan-outs / lots of independent stages are an issue. Currently, MultiPhaseFusion will sequenialize such wide fan-out DAGs, which increases compile times and renders downstream HorizontalFusion infeasible. The desired end state is supporting spatial partitioned concurrent execution of independent stages (up to the thread block cluster limit) within MultiPhaseFusions.

For now, require every stage added in `TryAddStage` to be reachability-ordered with all existing stages in the candidate DAG, keeping `BuildPhaseDag` intact so this
check can be replaced by an ALAP list scheduler later.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Harden CPU runtime thunks against buffer bounds, aliasing, queue, and PRED bugs

- Validate shapes, dense byte layouts, slice sizes, and `TransposePlan` creation in `CopyThunk`, and handle overlapping copies and transposes without races or corruption.
- Validate dense layouts, slice sizes, dimensions, overlapping inputs, and null `function_library` in `SortThunk`, and stage misaligned slices into aligned scratch storage.
- Validate dimensions, byte size overflow, slice sizes, and output aliasing in `TopKThunk`, and snapshot overlapping input slices in `internal::TopK`.
- Release dequeued `XfeedBuffer` entries before returning errors and guard zero length and null pointers in `InfeedThunk` and `OutfeedThunk`.
- Validate branch counts and negative `trip_count`, read `PRED` buffers via `uint8_t != 0`, and load `S32` branch indices via `std::memcpy` in `ConditionalThunk` and `WhileThunk`.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Do not offload 8-bit integer arithmetic to YNNPACK

With default flags, porting a `uint8` image pipeline to JAX on CPU gives
results that differ from NumPy and XLA:GPU as soon as the inputs are large
enough to be fused into a `__ynn_fusion`. For example:

```python
f = jax.jit(lambda a, b: jnp.max(a, axis=0, keepdims=True) + b)
f(np.full((1024, 17), 255, np.uint8), np.full((1024, 17), 103, np.uint8))
```

returns `255` instead of `102`, and in a `uint8` contrast stretch 50-89% of
the pixels on 480x640 frames are wrong. `s8` `127 + 1` gives `127` instead of
`-128`, and `s8` `7 / 2` gives `4` instead of `3`. XLA:GPU, NumPy,
`HloEvaluator`, constant folding and XLA:CPU on small (unfused) inputs all
wrap and truncate.

Reported by @SomyaPadhy4501 in https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/51826
(found while porting an image pipeline, and also by a CPU-vs-GPU integer
fuzzer).

Root cause: `IsElementwiseOpSupportedByYnn` accepts `S8`/`U8` for every op in
`GetYnnBinaryOpMap()` and `GetYnnUnaryOpMap()`. YNNPACK's 8-bit add, subtract,
multiply and power saturate and its integer divide rounds. It has no 8-bit
unary kernels, so it computes them in fp32 and saturates the result (`u8`
`negate(1)` gives `0`, `s8` `negate(-128)` and `abs(-128)` give `127`). Any of
these ops fused next to a YNN reduction (the default `REDUCE` fusion type)
changes the result.

Fix: for `S8`/`U8` binary ops, only offload `maximum` and `minimum`, and for
`S8`/`U8` unary ops, only offload `convert` and `sign`. These give the same
results either way. Other 8-bit elementwise ops fall back to the regular
XLA:CPU emitter. Floating-point ops, integer reductions and converts are
unchanged. This follows the earlier fixes that stop offloading ops
YNNPACK cannot compute exactly (#48378, #49899).

Tested: new `YnnReduceInt8EltwiseTest.EltwiseAfterReduceWraps` in
`//xla/backends/cpu/transforms:ynn_matcher_test` runs the issue's pattern
(max/min reduce + broadcast + add/subtract/multiply/divide/power on `u8`/`s8`
`[1024,17]`), and new `YnnReduceInt8UnaryTest.UnaryBeforeReduceWraps` runs
`negate`/`abs` feeding a max reduce. All 9 cases fail before this change (255
vs 102, 127 vs -128, 0 vs 255, 127 vs -56, 4 vs 3, 127 vs -128, 0 vs 255, 127
vs -128, 127 vs -128) and pass after it. Both tests also check with
`MatchOptimizedHlo` that only the reduce stays in `__ynn_fusion`.
`YnnReduceTest.Int8MaximumAfterReduceIsFused` checks that `s8` maximum is
still fused into `__ynn_fusion`.

display_title: [XLA] Fix unsound rewrites and crashes in TreeReductionRewriter

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Fix unsound rewrites and crashes in TreeReductionRewriter

Require associative reducers with exact scalar identity initial values, or idempotent associative reducers, before splitting a reduction into a padded `reduce-window` and an outer `reduce`. Skip nonpositive or unit window sizes, variadic or mixed precision reductions, unbounded dynamic shapes, and dynamic or zero sized reduced dimensions. Preserve subbyte `element_size_in_bits`, instruction metadata, and control dependencies across the rewrite, and instantiate the rewrite visitor per computation.
